title: Adopt new test evaluators through explicit advisory and required profiles

fields.outcome: A repository can start collecting visible results from a newly wired test evaluator before explicitly making that evaluator a required gate.
fields.scope: Use the existing named-profile and per-check required flag to represent advisory and enforced stages. Document and, where selected, generate both profile entries from the module wiring flow. A repository-owner comment or ADR may record that the milestone was reached or deferred; promotion remains a reviewed configuration, policy, or CI change.
fields.acceptance: Advisory failures stay visible without a successful result implying approval; the required profile blocks on the same failure; promotion is explicit and traceable.
fields.decisions: ADR-0013 assigns milestone declaration and deferral to the repository owner. A comment or ADR is intent evidence, not a signed decision. Active work keeps its frozen snapshot, warns about affected policy changes, and asks whether to adopt the new revision.
fields.verification: Evaluate the same failing and passing evaluator under advisory and required profiles, verify required organization checks cannot be weakened, and verify old configurations retain their behavior.
fields.dependencies: Implemented with module evaluator wiring. Automatic silent promotion remains out of scope.
fields.risks: A profile name alone does not enforce which profile CI selects; boundary enforcement still requires the repository's trusted CI or equivalent integration.
fields.changes: Implemented optional owner promotion metadata, incomplete results for deferred enforced profiles, advisory/required module profiles, and session policy-drift reporting that preserves the frozen snapshot.
fields.evidence: Evaluation and session tests cover deferred promotion, advisory/required behavior, policy digest drift, and unchanged frozen snapshots.

criteria.expectation: A failing evaluator configured with required false remains visible in reports and does not by itself make the requested advisory profile fail.
The same failing evaluator configured as required produces the documented nonzero result in the enforced profile.

Moving repository CI or configuration from the advisory profile to the enforced profile is an explicit reviewable change linked to the repository-owner comment or ADR that reached or deferred the milestone.
A profile cannot omit or downgrade an organization-required check, and neither profile creates or implies a signed governance decision.
Existing profiles and frozen snapshots keep their current meaning until a consumer explicitly adopts the new profile configuration.
When policy changes during active work, the user sees the new revision and affected checks and is asked whether to adopt it; the active frozen snapshot is not silently replaced.
A noninteractive run encountering an unadopted policy change reports the mismatch and required action without selecting a policy revision or claiming success.
